text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, A08 appears in about 30 in 100 traces, up from about 13 in 100 earlier (59 vs 26 of 200 traces), and it occurs earlier within traces: its mean relative position fell from about 0.49 to about 0.34 with a much narrower spread (standard deviation about 0.32 to 0.16). It also follows the early, recurring A16 far more often (about 21 vs 5 in 100 traces). [OCC008, POS001, REL001]
- The hand-over after A45 changed: earlier, about 92 in 100 of A45's outgoing transitions went directly to A26; in the later window they go to A08, A19, A20 and A25 in roughly equal quarter shares, and A26 now follows A45 two to three positions later (about 73 in 100 at two steps) instead of immediately (about 91 in 100 at one step earlier). [DIR045, LAG027, LAG026]
- A19, A20 and A25, which earlier ran after A26/A27/A28, now run before them: earlier, A26 preceded A19 in about 31 in 100 traces and A19 preceded A26 in almost none; later, A19 precedes A26 in about 35 in 100 and never the reverse, with the same reversal against A27 and A28 for A20 and A25, while the share of traces containing both activities stayed roughly stable (about 32 vs 35 in 100 for A19 and A26). [REL030, REL031, REL036, REL037, REL041, REL042, REL043]
- Their successors changed accordingly: earlier, A19, A20 and A25 led mainly to A28 and A32 (about half each); in the later window nearly all of their outgoing transitions go to A26 (about 96–100 in 100), and A19 reaches A26 in one step in about 69 traces where earlier the pair appeared at four steps in a single trace. [DIR019, DIR020, DIR025, LAG014]
- The loop around A28 disappeared and A27 → A28 → A32 tightened: earlier, A28 led back to A19/A20/A25 in about half of its outgoing transitions and A27 led to them in about 46 in 100; later, A27 leads to A28 in about 98 in 100 and A28 to A32 in about 99 in 100 of their transitions, the old close spacings A28→A25 and A25→A32 (previously about 41 and 72 traces) are nearly absent, and A27 reaches A32 in two steps rather than three. [DIR028, DIR027, LAG022, LAG016, LAG018, LAG023, LAG019]
- A08 now occupies a fixed slot in this hand-over: about one step after A45 (52 supporting observations vs 4 earlier), one step before A19/A20/A25, and about two steps before A26 (about 96 in 100); earlier its outgoing transitions were spread over many activities with none above about 14 in 100. [LAG026, LAG002, LAG003, DIR008, REL006, REL010]
- Positions shifted consistently: A19, A20 and A25 moved much earlier (mean relative position about 0.59–0.61 down to about 0.32–0.33), A26, A27 and A28 moved slightly later (for example A26 about 0.32 to 0.35), and downstream of A16 the block is reached later (A26 at four to five steps instead of about three; A19 at three to five steps in about 64 traces where earlier the pair appeared at a fixed lag in one trace). [POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, LAG009, LAG008]
- Participation also shifted elsewhere: A18 fell from about 32 to 20 in 100 traces (64 to 40 of 200) and co-occurs less with A26/A27/A28/A32/A45; A17 rose slightly; A44, A46 and A47 show modest increases in participation and within-trace repetition (for example A46's mean occurrences about 1.56 to 1.69 with recurrence support about 0.32 to 0.45); and the rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A10 each roughly halved (for example A02 from 20 to 9 traces). [OCC018, REL023, OCC017, OCC040, OCC041, OCC042, OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the segment between A45 and A26 runs in a different order: A45 now hands over to A08, A19, A20 or A25, and these activities execute before A26, whereas earlier A45 handed over directly to A26 and A19, A20 and A25 executed later, after A27/A28, feeding a loop with A28 and A32. A08, previously occasional with scattered successors, is now a regular member of this group (about 13 to about 30 in 100 traces), typically running directly after A45 and before A19/A20/A25; the loop through A28 is gone, leaving a tight A27 → A28 → A32 sequence. [DIR045, DIR008, DIR019, DIR020, DIR025, DIR027, DIR028, REL030, REL006, LAG027, LAG014, LAG019, OCC008]

The support is direct and consistent: successor profiles changed at A45, A19, A20, A25, A27 and A28; the pairwise order between the two groups flipped while their co-occurrence stayed roughly stable; distances changed in matching ways; and positions moved in the predicted directions. The difference concentrates in this hand-over region — downstream of A26 the successor structure is essentially unchanged (A26 still leads mainly to A37 and A38). Limitations: the many items are facets of the same traces rather than independent confirmations, and with 200 traces per window, small share changes elsewhere may be sampling variation. [DIR045, DIR019, REL030, LAG027, LAG019, POS004, POS007, DIR026]

An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a shift in the mix of pre-existing trace variants — for example, traces in which this group already ran before A26 becoming more frequent — which would produce the same relational signatures without any activity being relocated; the aggregate indicators cannot distinguish these. The decreases in the rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A10 also rest on only about 7–26 traces per window and may be rare-variant noise. [OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC010]

Other differences: outside the reordered segment, A18 participation fell from about 32 to 20 in 100 traces while A17 rose slightly (about 21 to 26 in 100); A44, A46 and A47 show modest increases in participation and repetition; and the rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A10 roughly halved with visibly changed successor profiles on very few observations (about 6–16 outgoing transitions per window), so these may reflect sampling variation of rare variants rather than the reordering. [OCC018, OCC017, OCC040, OCC041, OCC042, OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC010, DIR002, DIR004, DIR006, DIR010]
